profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company, traded under the ticker CRNC and headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts. Its site describes it as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, work the company says is powered by CaLLM, its family of language models, to enable natural, multimodal and safe interactions. The company also states it is moving to advance generative AI and large language model-powered innovation that it believes will be central to the automotive and transportation user experience, and it describes offering tailor-made AI solutions that integrate with vehicle makers' own brands.

Among the products described on the site is Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection, or EVD, which the company says is already deployed in production vehicles. Cerence says EVD detects and localizes more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, identifying approaching emergency vehicles from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters when paired with exterior microphones. The site also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, which lets passengers in different zones make requests at the same time while keeping recognition quality consistent across front and rear seats. In its third quarter results, the company reported revenue up 12% YoY and connected services revenue up 20% YoY, with operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program. Site material also covers work with Microsoft on Zero Trust Architecture for in-car assistants, credited to Kaivan Karimi, Business Development Senior Director at Cerence AI, and Frank Kaleck, Director Industry Advisory Automotive at Microsoft, and a speech enhancement demo credited to Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich.

The company's SEC filing identifier is 0001768267. No individual lawsuits are named for Cerence, and its law exposure is concentrated in Massachusetts with a count of 176.
